analysis.object_name: Small round cafe table with black molded side chairs
analysis.summary: Primary foreground objects are a small round table and three matching black side chairs arranged against a white wall on carpet; scope is the seating set as the most prominent foreground furniture, excluding wall, floor, glass partition and bottle as surrounding props.

components.name: Molded chair shell - seat and backrest
components.function: Provides seated support surface for occupant
components.evidence: Glossy black one-piece contoured shell with curved upright backrest and integrated seat clearly visible on middle chair, with matching shape on left and partial right chair, light reflection along edge

components.name: Chair leg frame - tubular metal legs
components.evidence: Four slender silvery tubular legs per chair extending from under shell to dark carpet, two front legs of middle chair prominently in foreground, rear legs partially visible

components.name: Round table top
components.function: Horizontal surface for placing small objects
components.evidence: Circular white surface with faint grey marbling and thin dark rim with gold-tone edge bevel, centered against wall with teal bottle resting on it

components.name: Table leg assembly - splayed legs
components.function: Supports table top and transfers load to floor
components.evidence: Three dark angled struts splaying outward from under tabletop to carpet, visible as matte black legs with slight taper

components.name: Leg foot caps
components.function: Contact point with floor, may protect flooring and add friction
components.evidence: Small gold-colored conical caps at tips of table legs, most distinct on right-front leg near carpet and faintly on rear leg

principles.name: Vertical load transfer to floor
principles.explanation: Visible form suggests weight on tabletop or chair seat would travel downward through respective legs to carpet; actual joint strength, fasteners, and load capacity are not visible and are inferred only from arrangement

principles.name: Stability from splayed footprint
principles.explanation: Angled table legs appear to widen the base relative to the top, which likely improves tipping resistance; effectiveness depends on hidden attachment rigidity and floor levelness not assessable in photo

principles.name: Shell curvature for rigidity
principles.explanation: Curved molded chair shell likely gains stiffness from its three-dimensional contour without visible additional bracing; material thickness and internal reinforcement are not visible

uncertainty: Exact materials, wall thickness, and manufacturing method of shells, tabletop, and legs cannot be determined from image
Internal construction, hidden fasteners, welds, or brackets attaching chair legs to shell and table legs to top are not visible
Precise dimensions, weight, weight rating, and stability on carpet are not measurable from this single perspective
Condition of undersides, hidden wear, cracks, or previous repairs not shown
Brand, age, and compliance with any safety standards not visible
Whether floor is level and furniture is stable cannot be judged from photo
next_steps: Take a closer eye-level photo of chair leg-to-shell junction from side to see attachment without moving furniture
Photograph underside of table if accessible without lifting, to observe leg bracket form
Capture a wider angle showing full right chair and surrounding partition for context
safety_notes: Photo alone cannot assess structural integrity, weight limits, or tip-over risk; do not stand on chairs or table
Check for wobble and loose joints in person before use; carpet may conceal uneven footing
Keep away from open flame or heat sources; material flammability unknown from image
